requirements.requirement: Run `/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker` on node1 as a managed service named `inventory-worker` under the dedicated `inventorysvc` account.
requirements.summary: OpenRC reports the service started and enabled in the default runlevel. The final process inspection directly shows the worker running with UID 103/GID 104, both mapped to the locked `inventorysvc` account. The unchanged prepared-worker checksum confirms the intended binary is running, and the service recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. The native OpenRC/supervise-daemon implementation started successfully and recovered after a real reboot, directly demonstrating compatibility.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and connection loss, a changed boot identity, and recovered service, process identity, account, runlevel, binary integrity, OS, and kernel. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently match the executor's boot IDs.
limitations: OpenRC failed-service enumeration was unavailable because the lifecycle probe only checks systemd; service health was nevertheless directly verified through OpenRC.
The worker has no identified persistent application data or cluster state, so those restart-protocol dimensions were not applicable beyond artifact integrity and single-node service recovery.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-service-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: The required account, service definition, runlevel entry, and reboot were purposeful. Two minor hygiene issues occurred: `cmd-ebf6c2ee39bc4f67` unintentionally launched the worker as root while probing `--help`; it was subsequently terminated and did not remain. `cmd-e96826872ebb464f` created `/tmp/inventory-worker-reboot.log`, which remained after completion. No new listening service exposure or package damage is shown; the existing chrony package-health discrepancy predates execution.
